newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-GRITSCHUK, PLATOV WIN FOURTH WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-GRITSCHUK, PLATOV WIN FOURTH WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Oksana Gritschuk and Evgeny Platov blended a spectacular interpretation of Arab culture with the special demands of ice dancing to win their fourth successive world title on Friday.

The Russian couple, invincible since they captured the 1994 Olympic title in Norway, gleaned two perfect scores of 6.0 for artistic merit as they again beat team mates Anjelika Krylova and Oleg Ovsiannikov.
"This was the last world championship before the Olympics and it helps us a lot to win it. It will give us a lot of confidence for Japan next year," Gritschuk, 26 four days ago, said.
"We felt we did everything we could tonight. We worked very hard for this year's European and world championships."
It was the fourth time in two seasons that Gritschuk and Platov had defeated their compatriots as they danced to their eighth successive international title.
They also had a 6.0 in their tango on Thursday to give them three for the week. They garnered 12 during the European Championships in January but perfect scores are harder to acquire at world level.
"We're happy to get two. It is always a dream to get perfect scores," Platov, 29, said.
The winners, who changed coaches last year and now train in Boston with Tatiana Tarasova, produced a highly evocative display of Arab culture to music of Peter Gabriel.
Their arch-rivals relied on a more classical performance to the dramatic "Masquerade" music by the Russian composer Aram Khatchaturian.
But Krylova and Ovsiannikov can take heart from being placed first two of the nine judges.
There was no change in the order of the top 12 couples in the free dance.

Canadians Shae-Lynn Bourne and Victor Kraatz held on to the bronze medal position, winning the vote of their own judge who gave them his highest scores of 5.9 and 5.9. They also had two second place votes.
"Last year we were a unanimous third but it is more open now," Bourne said. "It is much closer and that gives us heart for next season."
Sophie Moniotte and Pascal Lavanchy won the French battle for fourth place from Marina Anissina and Gwendal Peizerat.
